speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin narrowing down the cause of these concerning symptoms, have you noticed if the lymph nodes are tender to the touch or if they have appeared suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms are very concerning; the combination of drenching night sweats, significant weight loss, and persistent abdominal pain suggests a serious underlying condition. Given your weight loss, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, or any blood in your stool? Also, have you recently experienced any fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fact that your supraclavicular lymph node is painless, fixed, and has recently appeared is a classic "B symptom" combination often associated with malignancies like lymphoma or metastatic cancer. To determine the origin, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing, shortness of breath, or unintentional night sweats that soak your clothes? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, ESR. REQUEST TEST: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC (Elevated), Hemoglobin (Slightly Decreased), Platelets (Normal); Lactate_Dehydrogenase (Elevated); CT_Scan_Thorax_and_Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy_Cervical_Lymph_Node: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Vital_Signs: Temperature (36.8°C), Blood_Pressure (135/80 mmHg), Heart_Rate (82 bpm), Respiratory_Rate (14 breaths/min). Physical_Exam: Nontender, enlarged, fixed supraclavicular lymph node; slight abdominal distension; splenomegaly without rebound tenderness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), elevated LDH, and a biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index is diagnostic.
